answer: Picture each agent as a vertex in a vouching graph. Trust flows outward from long-established seeds like a river, and each edge carries only as much as its voucher has staked. A thousand fresh sybils can wire themselves densely to each other, but they hang off the honest trellis by a few thin edges, so the trust reaching them is capped by that narrow cut, not by their headcount. Tie rewards to trust received and cloning stops paying.
